subject.title: fix(qqbot): allow approval buttons in direct C2C conversations

question: For QQBot C2C approval buttons without execApprovals, is possession of a direct-chat button sufficient authority, or must the callback actor match a configured or approval-bound trusted identity?
rationale: The existing gate deliberately treats fallback approvals as security-sensitive, while this PR assumes a QQ platform recipient-binding guarantee that is neither encoded nor proven; choosing the permanent trust boundary requires owner intent.

options.title: Require an approval-bound identity
options.body: Keep a trusted actor check and accept C2C callbacks only when the sender matches the configured owner or the identity bound to the delivered approval.

options.title: Trust direct button possession
options.body: Accept the unconditional C2C bypass only after explicitly documenting and proving that QQ callbacks cannot come from anyone except the approval-message recipient.

recommendation.title: Require an approval-bound identity
recommendation.body: Keep a trusted actor check and accept C2C callbacks only when the sender matches the configured owner or the identity bound to the delivered approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the current fallback-approval authorization boundary and its security rationale.
